Image: © Photowitch | Dreamstime.com
By Charlotte Goldstone
16 November 2026
The relationship between vessel utilisation and container spot freight rates is markedly different on the transpacific and Asia-Europe trades.
New analysis from Sea-Intelligence raises questions over how reliably capacity utilisation can predict pricing.
The analyst found a strong correlation between utilisation and spot rates on the transpacific, where freight rates rise sharply once vessel utilisation exceeds 90%.
However, the relationship is considerably weaker on Asia-Europe, where transhipment activity and geopolitical disruptions complicate the traditional supply-demand equation.
Sea-Intelligence compared Drewry’s World Container Index (WCI) spot rates with demand data from Container Trade Statistics (CTS) and capacity figures from its own Trade Capacity Outlook database. The analysis used monthly averages, with September’s the latest data available, and calculated utilisation by dividing loaded cargo volumes by nominal vessel capacity.
Source: Sea-Intelligence
On the transpacific, the analysis identified a clear relationship between utilisation and freight rates, with the strongest correlation, 71%, occurring when spot rates lagged changes in utilisation by one month.
It said this suggested capacity utilisation was a significant driver of spot rate movements, although other factors also influenced pricing.
Source: Sea-Intelligence
A further analysis of utilisation against spot rates showed freight rates begin climbing steeply once utilisation passes 90%, reflecting a tightening capacity market in which shippers compete for available slots.
Source: Sea-Intelligence
The picture on Asia-Europe was markedly different, however, where Sea-Intelligence found a much weaker relationship between utilisation and freight rates, even after applying three-month rolling averages to smooth out short-term volatility.
Its correlation analysis and scatter plot showed changes in nominal vessel utilisation were a poor indicator of spot rate movements on the trade, which the analyst suggested reflected fundamental differences in the structure of the two trades.
Source: Sea-Intelligence
On the transpacific, most vessel capacity is dedicated to cargo moving between Asia and North America, making utilisation a relatively direct measure of the balance between supply and demand, while Asia-Europe is more complex, as vessels carry cargo for multiple markets through major transhipment hubs along their routes.
Consequently, capacity that appears available on the main Asia-Europe trade may already be committed to cargo moving on other tradelanes.
The analyst also highlighted the impact of the Red Sea and Hormuz crises on vessel deployment, further distorting the relationship between nominal capacity, actual utilisation, and freight rates.
Sea-Intelligence acknowledged that its utilisation calculations had limitations, as nominal capacity did not necessarily reflect the actual space available for cargo, while carriers do not disclose precisely how vessel capacity is allocated between trades.
The findings suggest that while utilisation can provide a useful signal of impending freight rate increases on the transpacific, applying the same metric to Asia-Europe risks overlooking significant operational and geopolitical factors influencing pricing.

To achieve a positive return, drugs launched from 2016 to 2020 must generate nearly $12 billion in sales, up from just $1.4 billion for drugs launched in the early 1990s.
About 90% of drugs launched from 2016 to 2020 are projected to generate insufficient lifetime revenues to cover their estimated costs, an IQVIA report found .
The report analyzed 825 novel medicines launched in the U.S. between 1991 and 2020. For each drug, IQVIA assessed lifetime revenues, operating costs, taxes and capitalized R&D spending to evaluate how returns on investment have changed over time. IQVIA found the share of medicines generating a positive return on investment has fallen to an all-time low.
About half of medicines launched in the early 1990s generated positive economic returns over their life cycles. That figure fell to fewer than one in 10 for the cohort of medicines launched between 2016 and 2020. None of the drugs launched in 2020 are forecast to generate a positive return.
Average lifetime returns have fallen throughout the past two decades. The average return for launches from 1991 to 1995 was $555 million. That figure held roughly steady over the following decade, falling slightly for the 1996 to 2000 cohort before climbing to $644 million for drugs launched between 2001 and 2005. But returns turned negative for drugs launched from 2006 to 2010, and by the 2016 to 2020 period lifetime revenue fell $1.7 billion short of total operating and R&D costs, on average.
The trend reflects a sharp increase in the sales a product needs to generate to achieve a positive return. For drugs launched from 1991 to 1995, sales needed to hit $1.4 billion to turn a profit; that number rose to $11.9 billion for the class of 2016 to 2020. IQVIA attributed the shift to shortening life cycles, stable operating costs, rising R&D spending and falling success rates.
Indeed, development costs have risen dramatically as revenues have dipped. Base-case capitalized R&D costs per new medicine were about $366 million in 1991. By 2020, that figure had risen to $3.2 billion. Median lifetime sales, meanwhile, fell from $1.5 billion for medicines launched between 1991 and 1995 to $1 billion for products that came to market between 2016 and 2020.
The median figure masks a wide gap between the most and least successful products. About 44% of the analyzed products generated less than $1 billion and accounted for 4% of aggregate industry revenues. About 10% of launches generated lifetime revenues of $10 billion or more. Those drugs accounted for 56% of industry revenues.

Jeep Recalls Nearly 390,000 SUVs and Trucks Over Faulty Uconnect 5 Infotainment Software
13 photos
Photo: Jeep
Stellantis has identified a software problem that affects a lot of sport utility vehicles and pickup trucks equipped with a certain type of Uconnect 5 radio unit. Referred to as the R1 High, said infotainment system can fail to display the rearview camera image.
Rather than the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, we learned about said recall from the Federal Motor Transport Authority of Germany. The Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt refers to said campaign as 16995R while Jeep calls it 78D. Suspect models include the Gladiator, Wrangler, Compass, Cherokee, Grand Cherokee, and Grand Wagoneer.
Affected vehicles were produced between May 22, 2025, and August 5, 2026, at multiple plants. Toledo is the stomping ground of the Gladiator and Wrangler, whereas the Grand Cherokee hails from the Detroit Assembly Complex. Warren is where Stellantis assembles the Grand Wagoneer, while Toluca serves as the home of the Cherokee and Compass.
Per the KBA, an estimated 119 vehicles were sold in the German market. Uconnect 5 handles a lot more than infotainment duties in these vehicles, including vehicle-related settings. The R1 High version is an Android-based affair that uses the Stellantis Atlantis electronic architecture, promising up to 5 times faster processing than Uconnect 4 systems.
When it comes to memory and storage, 6 gigs of RAM and no more than 64 gigs of solid-state flash storage are on the menu. Uconnect 5 and the R1 High version support a bunch of display configurations, including landscape and portrait screens running at 720P to ultra-HD resolution.
Photo: Jeep When the driver selects reverse, the rearview image may not be displayed on the central screen, and this problem is a noncompliance in the eyes of the NHTSA in the United States market. Speaking of which, 26V531 is what the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration calls the recall.
The US population is estimated at 844,028 vehicles because it extends beyond the Jeep brand. Other nameplates that carry the subject infotainment software include the Chrysler Pacifica and Voyager, Dodge Charger, Ram HD, Ram 1500, and the Ram ProMaster line of large vans. In the United States, customer notifications were mailed back in September 2026.
Radio software can be updated either at the dealer of your choice or by using the over-the-air capability of the Uconnect 5 R1 High system. The issue further affects 82,869 vehicles in Canada, 7,969 in Mexico, and 15,736 vehicles sold outside North America. The 389,577 figure presented by the KBA concerns European markets.
In the Old Continent, affected customers are required to get in touch with an authorized Jeep service partner. Owners of privately imported or gray-market vehicles without EC type approval must contact their importer. Dealers and importers are required to verify the software version.
The software update must be copied to a USB flash drive with at least 4 gigs to its name, and the installation can only proceed by connecting the wiTECH micro pod II or MDP device to the data link connector. The final step is to clear all DTCs, as you'd expect from a software-only job.

VW ID. Cross Goes on Sale, Here’s How Much the Zero-Emission Baby SUV Costs
6 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
Subsequent to the official unveiling hosted this summer, the Volkswagen ID. Cross hit the assembly line at the Pamplona factory in Navarra, Spain, in September, and now it is ready to go on sale in the United Kingdom.
The company’s local branch recently announced that the order books will officially open on November 19, albeit for the 52 kWh battery pack versions, as the cheaper ones, which feature a 37 kWh battery pack will go on sale in January 2027.
Thus, the only versions that will be available starting later this week will be the Life and Style 52 kWh, with the former starting at 30,260 pounds (equal to $43,930) and the latter at 33,675 pounds ($44,480) on-the-road, including VAT. VW says that the 52 kWh models are eligible for the electric car grant (£1,500 / $1,980), and qualification for the 37 kWh versions is still awaiting confirmation.
As for the 37 kWh -equipped variants of the 2026/2027 Volkswagen ID. Cross , these will also be available in the Life and Style trim levels. Pricing for the former will kick off at 26,985 pounds ($35,640), OTR, including VAT, and the latter will start at 30,400 pounds ($40,150).
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen’s ID. Cross equipped with the 37 kWh battery pack can be charged at up to 88 kW, whereas the 52 kWh option can sip electrons at up to 105 kW. The lesser model is said to have a combined WLTP-rated range of 194 miles (312 km), and the superior one can travel up to 265 miles (426 km), the company says. A 10-80 percent recharge is said to take 23 minutes. The former has 135 ps (133 hp/99 kW) to play with, and the latter enjoys 211 ps (208 hp/155 kW).
Strangely, the press release shared at the bottom of the page does not reveal the equipment of the ID. Cross , and neither does the company’s official UK website. However, the configurator does, and that’s how we were able to find out that the model comes with stuff such as 7x18-inch alloys (Edinburgh), LED headlights, a reversing camera, keyless entry and go, a two-zone air conditioning system, a wireless charging pad, Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and ambient lighting.
The electric crossover also features four USB-C ports, two at the front and two at the rear, a six-speaker sound system, digital radio, a 12.9-inch infotainment screen, and plenty of safety gizmos. These include the automatic emergency braking with pedestrian and cyclist monitoring, adaptive cruise control, advanced driver attention and drowsiness monitoring, lane keeping assist, and others.
Opt for the Style trim level versions of the 2026/2027 Volkswagen ID. Cross , and the electric crossover will come with 8x19-inch alloys (Sevilla), LED matrix headlights, a navigation system, a heated multi-function steering wheel, sports comfort seats at the front with heating, and a 30-color ambient lighting system.
It also sports stainless steel pedals, the same sound system, infotainment, USB-C ports, auto-dimming rearview mirror, two-zone air conditioning system, reversing camera, front and rear parking sensors, and the same safety gizmos, the configurator reveals.
Photo: Volkswagen Things such as the energy-efficient heat pump, 3-pin charging cable, Technology Package (Style), rear tinted windows, panoramic glass roof, Seat Comfort Package, removable and lockable tow bar, Harman Kardon sound system, Mistral Crystal Gray-Natural White upholstery, and others are available.
Volkswagen’s ID. Cross is 4,153 mm (163.5 inches) long, which means that its footprint is similar to that of the T-Cross . However, it won’t cannibalize it, because the T-Cross is an ICE-powered model, whereas the ID. Cross is fully electric, as we already told you. It is built on the MEB+ construction, just like the ID. Tiguan, as well as the Cupra Raval, and the Skoda Epiq and Peaq.
The VW T-Cross, on the other hand, shares its old MQB A0 construction with the demised Audi A1, the SEAT Arona, Ibiza, Skoda’s Kamiq, Scala, Fabia, Slavia, the Mk6 VW Polo, and others.
Following in the footsteps of the ID. Polo and ID. Polo GTI , the Volkswagen ID. Cross is pretty much a high-riding alternative to the battery-electric Polo, and takes on the likes of the Renault 4 and Kia EV2. It offers 475 liters (16.8 cu-ft) of storage behind the rear seats, which is a 20-liter (0.7 cu-ft) improvement over the gasoline T-Cross, and the cargo area increases to 1,345 liters (47.5 cu-ft) with the rear seats folded down. The model has a towing rating of up to 1,200 kg (2,645 lbs).
As previously mentioned, the order books for the Volkswagen ID. Cross will officially open in the United Kingdom later this week, on November 19, 2026, albeit for the 52 kWh variants only, as the 37 kWh versions will go on sale in January 2027. And as you likely suspect, the car manufacturer does not intend to bring this model to the United States of America. But should they?

Plain sailing for CMA CGM’s shipping business, but an uphill climb for Ceva. AI-generated image
By Alex Lennane
16 November 2026
CMA CGM’s shipping profits surged in the third quarter – but its expanding logistics business earned less on more revenue, underlining the task facing Ceva’s new management.
For context, Maersk generated $519m of logistics EBITDA on $4.49bn of revenue, compared with CMA CGM’s $366m on $5.46bn.
Although the pair have different business mixes and acquisitions, Ceva enters its latest restructuring with CMA’s logistics division growing faster – and earning less than its Danish rival.
Across the group, CMA CGM’s revenue rose 31.1%, to $18.4bn, EBITDA increased 61.6%, to $4.78bn, and net profit more than tripled, to $2.32bn.
Shipping carried the improvement: volumes increased 5.5%, to 6.51m teu, and revenue per teu rose 30%, to $1,891. Shipping EBITDA reached $4bn, with a margin of 32.4%.
Chairman and chief executive Rodolphe Saadé said: “We are determined to pursue our investments to strengthen our market positions and keep providing innovative solutions to our customers.”
CMA identified restocking, AI infrastructure, and Chinese clean-technology and electric vehicle exports as demand drivers. It expects strong volumes and freight rates to persist, but warned of geopolitical and trade policy uncertainty.
A source close to the group told AFP that companies, particularly in the US, had been rebuilding inventories since Q2 as a precaution against conflict, oil-price, and tariff uncertainty. The source also pointed to the industrial components needed to build data centres as a source of container demand.
In logistics, revenue increased 19.2%, but EBITDA declined 14.4%, reducing the margin from 9.3% to 6.7%. CMA attributed the pressure to “difficult forwarding conditions and automotive sector weakness”.
Acquisitions also supported the logistics division’s expansion. AFP identified contributions from Borusan, Fagioli, and Fattal’s distribution businesses, now branded Tamina, although their individual contributions were not disclosed.
Maersk’s Logistics & Services division, by comparison, increased revenue by 12.7% and EBITDA by 10.9%. Its EBITDA margin remained broadly stable, at 11.6%, against 11.7% a year earlier. Forwarding improved its EBIT margin, from 3.5% to 4.3%, supported by strong air and project logistics volumes – something of a counterpoint to CMA’s description of forwarding market difficulties, although the companies have different exposures.
For Ceva, the quarter provides the starting point for CEO Patrick Moebel’s overhaul . As The Loadstar Premium previously reported , Mr Moebel told senior leaders that “clear pain points” were slowing the business and contributing to performance below industry standards and internal expectations.
The proposed changes consolidate activities around freight management and contract logistics, strengthen regional accountability, and move decisions closer to customers. Future organisation and reporting lines were to be implemented no later than 1 January 2027, subject to applicable consultation processes.
Mr Moebel’s ambition is to generate more than $1bn of “additional value” over three years, although the financial measure behind that target remains unclear.
There is more integration work ahead. CMA CGM completed its $1.4bn acquisition of FedEx Supply Chain on 1 October, adding a further business that did not contribute to the latest results.
The deal also involved aircraft moving in the opposite direction. Cargo Facts reported on 11 November that FedEx had acquired two CMA CGM 777 freighters as part of the transaction. A FedEx spokesperson linked the purchase to its MD-11F replacement strategy.
CMA’s quarterly update describes eight aircraft operating under its Air Cargo and Air Belgium brands, supported by hubs in France, Belgium and the US.
Standalone air cargo financial results were not disclosed. The Air Cargo and Terminals division contributed to growth in “other activities”, where revenue increased 27.1%, to $1.51bn, and EBITDA rose 41.9%, to $413m. CMA cited the solid momentum of both businesses.
FedEx Supply Chain’s contribution will begin to appear in Q4, while the operating overhaul is due by January. Subsequent results will show whether Ceva can accompany its next increase in scale with a recovery in profitability.

Backed by Novartis’ venture arm, El Lilly and CRISPR Therapeutics, Seawolf is advancing its nonviral DNA delivery platform while inking a pact with Sanofi.
Seawolf Therapeutics is unleashing with $100 million, while also spearing an up to $1.2 billion alliance with Sanofi to develop new redosable DNA medicines.
The San Diego biotech’s series A included support from founding investor Versant Ventures, plus Novartis Venture Fund (NVF), Eli Lilly, CRISPR Therapeutics and others, according to a Monday news release.
Seawolf has emerged wielding a Trident—the biotech’s DNA delivery platform. The redosable lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-based system is designed to deliver DNA-based payloads made to last longer than RNA-based LNP therapies while matching their potency, safety and scalability. Animal testing has shown that the nucleic acid-based therapies are potent, durable and have a clean safety profile, according to Seawolf.
While Trident can be deployed across a range of therapeutic areas, Seawolf’s lead program is designed to address metabolic diseases. The company did not share other specifics regarding its lead asset.
Seawolf has also reeled in a multi-target research and exclusive licensing deal with Sanofi, as disclosed in the same release. The duo will work to develop undisclosed therapies for bleeding disorders and other indications, with Seawolf eligible to receive up to $1.2 billion in biobucks, plus tiered royalties on potential sales related to the alliance.
“Seawolf is charting a new course in patient care through non-virally delivered DNA,” Seawolf CEO Elizabeth Alcamo said in the release. Alcamo was a former entrepreneur in residence for Versant and held senior roles at CODA Biotherapeutics and 4D Molecular Therapeutics before that.

MP Materials' Mountain Pass rare earths mine in southern California is the only rare earths producer in the United States. Credit: MP Materials
By: Northern Miner Staff November 16, 2026
Some mining stories deserve a second look because their significance wasn’t fully appreciated at the time. Taking a cue from The New York Times ’ obituaries of people overlooked in its earlier coverage, this instalment of From the Archives revisits California’s Mountain Pass mine. Its role in building America’s rare earth industry deserves renewed attention as the United States seeks to reclaim that industrial strength.
Before rare earths became a source of friction between Washington and Beijing, a California mine helped bring a brighter red into the world’s living rooms.
Mountain Pass, in the Mojave Desert southwest of Las Vegas, supplied europium for the phosphors used in colour television screens. During the 1960s, an expanding consumer market helped turn a deposit discovered by uranium prospectors into a leading source of minerals whose names few viewers would have recognized.
“The most important invention in the evolution of Mountain Pass was the commercialization of color television in the mid-1960s,” a 2007 U.S. Geological Survey account of the deposit’s geology and history noted. For this instalment of From the Archives , we’re revisiting a development whose significance deserves a fuller look: America’s rise as a rare earth supplier, decades before securing those materials became an urgent national priority.
Unexpected find
The discovery came in 1949, when prospectors searching California’s Clark Mountain Range for uranium encountered a radioactive anomaly. What they found was a deposit containing bastnaesite, a mineral rich in rare earth elements.
Molybdenum Corp. of America acquired claims and began small-scale rare earth production in 1952. The early operation was assembled partly from equipment brought from elsewhere, including a ball mill and flotation cells from the company’s Urad molybdenum property in Colorado.
But having a deposit was only the beginning. The commercial breakthrough depended on finding customers for its contents and developing ways to separate them.
Europium provided an opening. Compounds containing the element could produce a brighter red in colour television screens, giving manufacturers a reason to seek dependable supplies.
In 1965, Molybdenum Corp. built a europium oxide plant at Mountain Pass. Rare earth concentrate production increased sixfold from the previous year to about 6.1 million lb., according to a technical report filed by today’s owner, MP Materials (NYSE: MP).
That expansion connected an unfamiliar corner of the periodic table with a highly visible technological change. Consumers bought televisions; behind the screens, demand was helping build a mining and chemical processing business in the desert.
Mountain Pass became the world’s principal source of rare earths between 1965 and 1995. The United States occupied a position in this industry that can seem improbable when viewed through today’s concerns about Chinese supply.
The reversal
The advantage didn’t endure.
Growing Chinese production pushed rare earth prices lower, while Mountain Pass faced environmental problems. Leaks from wastewater pipelines drew regulatory scrutiny. The separation plant shut in 1998, followed by the suspension of mining in 2002.
The orebody remained. What had weakened was the business around it.
An investor group acquired Mountain Pass from Chevron (NYSE: CVX) in 2008. A new Molycorp pursued its revival, restarting active mining in December 2010 and undertaking a major modernization.
The return proved difficult. Production took longer to ramp up than expected, reducing revenues and cash flow, the company disclosed in its 2013 annual report. Molycorp filed for bankruptcy protection in June 2015, and Mountain Pass was subsequently idled.
MP Materials acquired and restarted the operation in 2017. Its effort has extended beyond extracting ore to restoring separation capabilities and building U.S. metal and magnet manufacturing.
The contrast with the television years became particularly clear in July 2025, when the U.S. Department of Defense announced an arrangement with MP Materials that included an equity investment, a loan commitment, a price floor for neodymium-praseodymium products and an agreement covering future magnet output.
Consumer demand had helped propel the earlier expansion. National security policy was now helping underpin another.
Mountain Pass’s history offers a caution against treating mineral leadership as a permanent consequence of geology. A rich deposit can support an industry, but processing expertise, customers, investment and workable economics determine whether it does.
The mine that helped brighten television screens deserves a place in that history. Long before Americans worried about recovering a rare earth supply chain, they had helped build one. Print

WARSAW, Poland — Estonia plans to close its road border crossings with Russia in response to an attempted arson attack against Estonian defense company Threod Systems that took place on Saturday, the country’s officials announced.
In the early hours of Nov. 14, Estonian law enforcement detained eight Latvian citizens suspected of attempting to set fire to the company’s facility in Viimsi, near the country’s capital, Tallinn, and cause an explosion.
“Based on an assessment of information from the Internal Security Service, this attack was carried out at the behest of the GRU, Russia’s military intelligence service,” Margo Palloson, the director general of the Estonian Internal Security Service (KAPO), was quoted in a statement released by the nation’s Prosecutor’s Office.
The facility did not sustain significant damage, as Threod Systems’ security personnel thwarted the attack in its initial phase, the office said.
Company spokeswoman Maarja Karin told Defense News there was no disruption in production activities.
“We are investigating the case under the provision of the Estonian Penal Code concerning activities directed against the security of the Republic of Estonia carried out on behalf of a foreign intelligence or security service, including gathering information or damaging property,” Estonian Prosecutor General Astrid Asi said in a statement issued by her office to Defense News.
In response to the sabotage attempt, the Estonian government will close Russian border crossings beginning on Dec. 1.
“Any attempt to threaten Estonia’s security, sow fear, or act hostilely against us will be met with a decisive response,” Estonian Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna was quoted in a statement released by his ministry. “Closing the border crossings will reduce Russia’s ability to conduct hostile activities against Estonia and help mitigate risks related to sanctions circumvention.”
Tsahkna said he would use a Nov. 16 meeting of the European Union’s foreign ministers in Brussels to discuss additional options aimed at Russia.
“As long as Russia continues its war of aggression against Ukraine and threatens European security, we must increase pressure on all fronts,” he said. “This means tougher sanctions, a stricter visa policy, and additional measures to limit Russia’s ability to pursue its objectives.”
Threod Systems produces a wide range of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), launcher systems for one-way drones, and electro-optical ISR and target acquisition systems. The Ukrainian military has successfully used the Estonian company’s drones and pneumatic launchers against invading Russian forces. This has put Threod Systems in Moscow’s crosshairs as Russia is scaling up its hybrid warfare attacks against European defense companies.
“Whenever you see a long-range drone hit a target inside Russia, it is likely that our launcher was used by the Ukrainian military to facilitate that,” a Threod Systems representative told Defense News at the 2025 DSEI UK show in London.
Alongside its deliveries to Ukraine, Threod Systems has also supplied its products to a number of militaries across the world, including in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Establishing a presence in the U.S. market has also been one of its goals, according to company representatives.
As the manufacturer has ramped up its export sales, this has also been accompanied by investments to expand its production capacities and turnover growth. For 2025, Threod Systems reported revenues of some €47.2 million ($52 million), an increase of 24.1% compared with a year earlier, and a profit of €15.6 million, up 76.4% year-on-year, as indicated by figures from the company.
The latest sabotage is part of a series of arson attacks targeting Estonia’s defense industry. On Aug. 15, a fire broke out at the premises of Milrem Robotics , an Estonian unmanned ground vehicle producer, in Tallinn. The same month, three suspects were arrested in Latvia on suspicion of carrying out the attack, and are currently in custody in Estonia.
In a Sep. 29 statement, intelligence officials said the attack had been “commissioned by Russian security services,” citing similarities between the perpetrators’ modus operandi and those of other similar attacks carried out in Europe on Moscow’s behalf.
“Defense industry companies, particularly those involved in drone technology, as well as organizations supporting Ukraine, have been among the targets of Russian security services since the beginning of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine,” KAPO head Palloson said.

MXGP 26 Review (PS5): It’s Fun for a While
40 photos
Photo: autoevolution
Is the motorcycle riding season over? Well, that depends. If you only ride road-going motorcycles and don’t live somewhere warm, it’s probably over. If you only ride off-road, there’s no such thing as a riding season in the first place. That has to be quite fun, and it has been on my mind for a few years now.
I’m an enduro/motocross rookie at best, as I have racked up more miles in professional drift cars than I have on those sort of motorcycles. As I live close to a mountain, everyone in my village seems to prefer this style. My nephew and brother-in-law have three of them in their garage, and I might just take up the offer to see what they’re like. Until then, the virtual world is my only “escape”, and I was somewhat excited to be testing MXGP 26 on my PS5 console.
I was instantly annoyed by the game’s prompt to log in before playing, until I noticed the Skip button on the bottom right. Selecting your racing game experience means choosing one of three options: Go Easy On Me, I Know My Stuff and I’m The Goat. I enjoying the framing of it all, and went for the middle option. Profile Creation is up next, and there’s a decent selection of gear for your rider. Right off the bat, the in-game music sounds generic at best.
It’s especially painful if you grew up with some of the racing games that came out in the late ‘90s and early 2000s. But I realize the soundtrack isn’t the most important part of a title like this, where the riding itself should be the key factor. The game offers a selection of multiple manufacturers at start including Beta, Ducati , Fantic, Kawasaki, Honda, Husqvarna, KTM and Yamaha.
You can switch between the MXGP, MX2, My 450CC and My 250CC categories depending on how slow or fast you want to go. I just selected the first bike and track combo I could find, only to discover I wasn’t nearly as prepared for the task ahead as I expected. Going off track will lead to an immediate reset, which turned out to be extremely annoying as I kept playing.
Where’s the freedom? Photo: autoevolution I understand I should get a penalty for going off-course, but having this virtual limit is a sure way of destroying any freedom you thought you had by playing the game. As things went so well with a slower bike, I figured I could just jump on one of MXGP Ducatis (with 63.5 hp on tap) and see what I was made of. There’s a decent selection of 19 tracks to choose from starting with Bariloche in Argentina, all the way to Darwin in Australia.
The MXGP South Africa layout is the longest at 1.24 miles/2,010 meters, while Loket in the Czech Republic features the most impressive altitude difference at 164 feet/50 meters. Talking about the type of soil in each location, the line-up includes sand, hard pack and clay, and I’m unsure which one is my favorite yet. I still haven’t gotten used to steering with the joystick, but I understanding implementing Gran Turismo 7 ’s model in motorcycle racing games isn’t that easy (or feasible at all).
Riding in Loket is pretty impressive, and the jumps are my favorite part. Thank God this game has a Photo Mode, even though the controls inside feel slightly counter intuitive to me. You can’t use photo mode when watching the replay, which seems downright silly if you ask me. The engine/exhaust note on the bikes isn’t great, but again, not a deal breaker either. I’d describe them as basic right now.
To me, the graphics look a bit outdated, which might be a consequence of playing on the PS5 and not on a PC. There’s not much time to really take in the scenery anyway, as you have to pay attention to the road ahead. Those ruts can hugely impact your results, but you can thankfully adjust that via the Terrain Deformation Quality settings. I wanted to see what the riding would be like with no traction or wheelie control, and it definitely made my life a lot harder.
Use the helmet cam! Photo: autoevolution I don’t remember ever falling off the bike as often in any other video game before. Switching back to “noob” mode made everything feel numb and I couldn’t quite live with that either. I switched to an entry-level Kawasaki for my next Time Trial attempt at Agueda in Portugal: it’s definitely the smart thing to do if you don’t fully grasp what racing in these conditions entails.
At this point I was having more fun than I did in NASCAR 26 , but the experience was still underwhelming at best. I moved on to Grand Prix mode, hoping that would make things a bit more exciting. It’s good to know that you can set up the bike the way you want it, changing things like the gear ratios, upshift power delivery, braking power, fork and shock stiffness among many other options.
I’m just as big of a rookie in that department as I am with riding these bikes, so I didn’t fiddle around with any of those options. Once you’re at the starting gate of a Grand Prix. Hitting the RPM sweet spot is pretty easy: it’s a feature some casual players might like, but I think it detracts from the realism of it all. The helmet cam is the best way to go if you want an extra dose of adrenaline, and the occasional splash of mud on the screen is fun.
Opting for the easiest level meant I was constantly ahead of my opponents despite crashing five times each lap. There’s no Riding School mode in the game, which is partly refreshing to see in a strange way. You do have the option to go to a training ground though, where there’s a bit more freedom to be experienced. You’re still left to figure it out on your own, which I don’t mind.
Photo: autoevolution I’m more upset about having such a small area to play in, especially when you think about how big the “world” is in GTA VI and even Assetto Corsa EVO ’s upcoming Free Roam mode. I kept thinking it’s not the kind of game I’d be desperate about playing at the end of a long day, but would I buy it?
I told myself: if it costs less than $30, it’s probably worth it if we have the certainty that the developer is planning to come up with some patches to improve the experience. Sadly, prices for a Steam Key are as low as 49.99 €, while you could pay up to 69.99 € on PS5 or Xbox. At this point you might as well get GTA VI instead and tour around on the dirt bikes inside without having to worry about ridiculous artificial limits.
Conclusion Nacon might be on to something here. MXGP 26 feels like an “Early Access” game with some potential for the future, but it’s still a fairly limited package for the price you have to pay.
I’m giving it a better rating than I did with NASCAR 26, but I’m bound to be annoyed if it shows up almost unchanged for 2027.
I wish the developers would focus on building it up for two or three years to the point where it gets constant, positive feedback from players worldwide. I want to believe it can be better, if only corporate greed doesn’t get in the way.
Rating: 65/100

BMW Classic Shows Off 1997 E38 M7 Packing E39 M5's S62 V8 Engine
20 photos
Photo: BMW Classic on Instagram / edited
Believe it or not, BMW actually built an E38-generation 7 Series with the M-specific naturally aspirated V8 engine of the M5 from that era. Also equipped with the Getrag-supplied manual transmission of the E39, the M7 in question has been recently brought into the open by the folks at BMW Classic.
The most interesting part of the M7 is how little BMW changed around it, keeping it as unassuming as possible both inside and out. Between you and me, the sleeper aesthetic is only natural when you learn that said prototype started life in the form of a 1997 model year 740i. That version of the E38 came with the non-M version of the naturally aspirated V8, namely the M62B44 engine.
S62B50 is what BMW calls the spicier powertrain, which displaces 4,941 cubic centimeters instead of 4,398 for the lesser V8. The S62 further upgrades to a forged steel crankshaft and conrods, partly because it was designed to rev higher. Low-friction pistons also need mentioning, with said lightweight units being critical to achieve the advertised 11.0:1 compression ratio.
Instead of a wet-sump lubrication system, the S62 of the E39 M5 upgrades to a semi-dry oiling setup that features two scavenge pumps. They pull engine oil back to the main sump during hard braking and cornering. Then there's double VANOS, the hollow camshafts, stiffer valve springs, and the dual-row timing chain.
Another way of separating the S62 from the M62 is to look at the intake system and throttle setup. Instead of a single MAF sensor, the M engine uses a dual-plenum airbox fed by two separate MAF sensors. Eight individual throttle bodies help the S62 stand out as well, representing a major upgrade from the lone throttle body of the M62B44 that powers the 1997 model year 740i.
Photo: BMW Classic on Instagram / edited Pictured with dark BBS wheels and four exhaust outlets that are connected to 4-2-1 tubular headers instead of log-style manifolds, the M7 is devoid of aerodynamic garnishing and swollen wheel arches. Hopping inside reveals a similar understated recipe, with BMW combining black and beige leather across the seats, dashboard, and door panels.
A three-spoke M steering wheel is on the menu, along with wood trim pieces around the center console and a phone in the rear center console. Tipping the scales at 4,134 pounds (1,875 kilograms) according to BMW Classic's Instagram post, the M7 is much obliged to match the E39 M5's top speed of 250 kilometers per hour (155 miles per hour).
Not bad for only 400 metric ponies, for sure! To develop those 394 mechanical horsepower, the S62 in the M7 has to reach 6,600 revolutions per minute. Why didn't BMW make a case for series production? We do not know for certain, but chances are the German automaker did not want the M7 to cannibalize sales of the naturally aspirated V12-powered 750i.
Nowadays, BMW offers two performance-oriented 7 Series models. The first one that comes to mind is the 2027 model year M760 xDrive, which is considered an M Performance model. That's also the case with the i7 M70 xDrive, albeit two electric motors drive both axles instead of xDrive and the S68 twin-turbo V8. Next year, BMW Alpina will add another layer to the performance-oriented 7 Series with go-faster models of its own. View this post on Instagram A post shared by BMW Classic (@bmwclassic)

Original Owner Lets Go of 1969 GTX After 317,000 Miles, "Completely Intact and Unmolested" Driver
23 photos
Photo: Hemmings/tommyscalera
"Reverent racing men have long called it The Boss. This year it'll be 'Boss, Sir.' And this year, it'll command even more respect. Because of styling and improved performance. Looks are as they should be. Competition-car clean, with just enough dress-up to keep the girls happy." That confident 1969 factory showroom brochure pitch heralded not a Ford Mustang, but an upscale Detroit Mopar heavyweight: the Plymouth GTX. Exactly like this one-owner survivor.
Introduced for 1967 as a Belvedere trim and built as a standalone model line from 1968 through 1971 before becoming a Road Runner option package until 1974, the GTX served as Plymouth's signature gentleman's muscle car. Riding on Chrysler's intermediate B-body platform, it blended big-inch (biggest, in fact) authority with upscale exterior trim, bucket-seat cabin comfort, and understated visual aggression.
The GTX offered discerning buyers a refined alternative to stripped-down street brawlers (like the Road Runner) without sacrificing genuine quarter-mile credibility. Unlike lesser intermediates, the GTX skipped small-block engines and basic big-block power entirely.
Its standard configuration paired Chrysler's 440-cubic-inch, 7.2-liter Super Commando V8, rated at 375 horsepower and 480 lb-ft of torque via a four-barrel carburetor, with the heavy-duty 727 TorqueFlite 3-speed automatic transmission. Buyers chasing maximum track supremacy could specify a floor-shifted 4-speed manual, the $119 440 Six-Barrel rated at 390 horsepower, or the $700 426 Street Hemi producing 425 horsepower.
Photo: Hemmings/tommyscalera Across its five-year run from 1967 to 1971, Plymouth built 44,178 GTX units for the United States domestic market, including 15,602 examples during 1969. That model year divided into 14,902 two-door hardtop coupes and 700 convertibles. Among those hardtops, 13,866 carried the standard 440 V8. Because 4,004 buyers chose the optional 4-speed manual, exactly 9,862 left the assembly line as 440-powered automatic coupes matching this particular survivor's specification.
Acquiring a brand-new 1969 Plymouth GTX hardtop required a base sticker price of $3,416 before options, positioning it $219 below the $3,635 convertible and well above the budget-oriented Road Runner. Nearly six decades later, an extraordinarily honest, one-owner California hardtop, originally assembled at Chrysler's Los Angeles facility, emerges from Simi Valley, California, preserving its numbers-matching big-block drivetrain and unmolested factory character intact.
The muscle car wears its original blue finish weathered into authentic California patina rather than fresh show paint. Its muscular, slab-sided B-body sheet metal remains completely intact and straight apart from minor, easily repaired fender dents. Factory glass survives clear and uncracked with functional roll-up windows, while the car rests on clean-looking tires that have aged past their safe service dates.
Photo: Hemmings/tommyscalera Inside the cabin, matching blue upholstery outfits the factory front bucket seats and center console in serviceable, driver-grade condition. All gauges and electrical accessories operate properly aside from the non-working air conditioning. However, decades of sun and regular use have left the headliner, carpet, and dash pad worn. There are, however, replacement components readily available.
Under the hood, the numbers-matching 440 Super Commando V8 resides in a stock, unmolested compartment alongside intact factory air-conditioning hardware. The chassis has accumulated a staggering 317,000 miles over its single-owner lifespan. The good news is the rebuilt 440 V8 and 727 TorqueFlite automatic have logged just 32,000 miles since their overhaul. The “Posi” rear axle is fitted with aggressive 4.11 gears (it’s Sure Grip, of course; Positive Traction, or Posi, was a GM nomenclature).
Recent mechanical attention ensures the big-block coupe remains road-ready for immediate cruising, or for gradual refurbishment. Freshly installed components include a new gas tank, fuel pump and sender unit, water pump, master cylinder, battery, and a newly rebuilt four-barrel carburetor.
Photo: Hemmings/tommyscalera Aside from fresh tires and servicing the intact air-conditioning system, the primary mechanical item awaiting attention is a replacement heater core, an inexpensive part priced around $58 from aftermarket suppliers.
Crucially for any vintage Mopar collector, lifelong dry-climate residency has spared the unibody structure from destructive corrosion. There is zero cancer or rust-through across the floorboards, fenders, or trunk pan, giving its next caretaker a remarkably solid foundation.
Whether preserved as a patina-clad weekend driver or stripped down for a concours-level restoration, an intact, one-owner, numbers-matching B-body coupe eliminates the structural guesswork that plagues heavily modified clones.
Photo: Hemmings/tommyscalera In the 2026 collector market, this survivor's pricing stacks up favorably against established valuation benchmarks for comparable cars - a $51,700 overall model median and a $99,000 median across 2026 auction sales skewed by restored and Hemi builds. Hagerty Marketplace 2026 transactions for 1969 GTX 440 automatic coupes sit at $38,739 and $56,000, and Classic.com tracks a $53,064 second-generation benchmark, placing this example comfortably below generational averages.
Offered as-is by a seller in Simi Valley, California, this one-owner 1969 Plymouth GTX 440 Super Commando hardtop is currently asking $44,750. Combining original Los Angeles assembly provenance, a freshly rebuilt numbers-matching big-block drivetrain, rust-free California sheet metal, and honest survivor aesthetics. If all the seller states about it in the Hemmings listing is correct, this unmolested golden-era Detroit muscle icon is a very accessible driver-level classic.

ULA Rocket Turns 40 Amazon Internet Satellites to Bits When It Fails During Ascent
8 photos
Photo: Amazon Leo
It's been a sort of explosive weekend for the American space industry, as two high-profile missions, executed by SpaceX and the United Launch Alliance (ULA), ended with spectacular failures. But whereas the explosion of the SpaceX Super Heavy as it came back to the pad was offset by the Starship doing exactly that, thus saving Flight 15, ULA's new Vulcan rocket failed completely and took a customer payload with it.
On Sunday, November 15, Space Launch Complex 41 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida witnessed the liftoff of a ULA Vulcan rocket loaded with 40 broadband Internet satellites for Amazon's Leo constellation (previously known as Project Kuiper).
The launch went without any issues, and everything (including engine cutoff and second stage ignition) seemed on track for the rocket's cargo to take its place in the network that will ultimately comprise some 3,000 satellites. Then, just ten minutes or so into the flight, the Vulcan failed, taking the 40 bits of hardware with it.
The incident is too fresh for ULA to know exactly what happened, so we'll have to probably wait a bit to learn what went wrong. For the rocket maker, the outcome could have a number of implications for the relatively new design.
Vulcan Centaur by its full name, on account of it using a Centaur V second stage, the rocket was first launched at the beginning of 2024, when it carried the Astrobotic Peregrine lunar lander on behalf of NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) program. Since then, it has flown three more times with no incident.
This weekend's launch was supposed to be the fifth, but also the first of no less than 38 Vulcan Amazon Leo missions. Before now, Amazon launched its satellites using the Atlas V, which flew to space eight times with this cargo on board.
Normally, the new Vulcan comes in four configurations, namely with zero, two, four, and six solid rocket boosters (SRBs). The version used this past weekend is the one with a low-Earth orbit-optimized configuration, the VC6L, which comprises six SRBs and a longer-length payload fairing.
The Vulcan first stage is 17.7 feet (5.4 meters) in diameter and stands 109.2 feet (33.3 meters) tall. It carries tanks to hold the liquefied natural gas (LNG) and methane fuel, and is equipped with a couple of BE-4 engines sourced from Blue Origin.
Each of the powerplants has a rating of 550,000 pounds of thrust at sea level, and is backed by six graphite epoxy motor (GEM) 63XL solid rocket boosters that deliver, each, 459,600 pounds of thrust.
The Centaur V second stage, on the other hand, has the same diameter (duh!), but is much shorter, at 35 feet (10.7 meters). It too carries fuel tanks, filled with liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen, which is sent to the two RL10C-1-1A engines strapped to it, each capable of developing 23,825 pounds of thrust. On its nose sits the payload fairing that comes in at 70 feet (21.3 meters) in this configuration.
When the Vulcan Centaur was announced, it was seen as a replacement for the Atlas 5 and Delta 4 families of rockets, and that continues to be so despite this recent failure. It's not clear at this point when the rocket will fly again, as that depends on the findings of the investigation into this weekend's mishap. We'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more. Based on data received by our Launch Director, we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit. Jaguar Land Rover Cuts 4,000 Salaried Jobs While China Sales Fall 45 Percent
31 photos
Photo: Land Rover
Tata Motors-controlled Jaguar Land Rover will be losing 4,000 salaried employees as part of the British automaker's latest restructuring program. The first 3,000 are already lined up, with most leaving at the end of November. These redundancies will purportedly save JLR around £400 million annually, but nevertheless, cutting payroll alone won't get the company back into shape.
Jaguar Land Rover generated £5.9 billion in revenue in the three months to September 30, yet its profit before tax and exceptional items amounted to a pitiful £6 million. Adding insult to injury, JLR recorded a staggering £530 million in exceptional charges, finishing the quarter with a £451 million loss after tax.
None other than chief financial officer Richard Molyneux confirmed the aforementioned figures during the Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Q2 FY27 earnings call. According to Molyneux, the remaining 1,000 employees should follow next year.
The £400 million that is supposed to be saved annually by cutting 4,000 jobs forms a large part of the wider Enterprise Missions savings program, which is estimated at £1.7 billion and runs over two years. Enterprise Missions also involves factory costs, structural efficiencies, and warranty expenses.
Jaguar Land Rover attributed £235 million of the reported £530 million in exceptional charges to postponed product investments and lower valuations for certain assets. To make matters worse for shareholders, revenue growth doesn't offer any sort of comfort either.
Photo: Land Rover Revenue remained flat in the analyzed quarter compared with the preceding one, with JLR delivering approximately 82,000 vehicles in the three-month period. The numbers we have right now also indicate that profitability deteriorated sequentially. More specifically, profit before tax and exceptional items nosedived from £109 million to £6 million, with the adjusted EBIT margin coming in at 1.1 percent.
Anyone in the biz is well aware that's a very thin cushion for a manufacturer specialized in expensive sport utility and electric vehicles. The cushion is thinner still when you remember that JLR is presently funding an extensive product renewal program that will see the introduction of a full-electric Jaguar sport utility vehicle.
China is part of the reason why Jaguar Land Rover wholesale volumes fell dramatically, with JLR confirming a 45 percent year-on-year nosedive during Q2 and 36 percent in the first half. Even the Middle East suffered from weak demand, albeit part of it can be explained by the logistical difficulties of the Iran war that also involves the Houthis, Hezbollah, and PMF.
JLR further recorded £540 million in free cash outflow during Q2, taking the first-half total to £1.5 billion. The cash balance stood at £1.8 billion on September 30, while total liquidity reached £6 billion, including undrawn credit facilities and loans. In other words, not all of those £6 billion is cash sitting in bank vaults.
Going forward, Jaguar Land Rover expects £1.25 billion in free cash outflow for the entire financial year. Its adjusted EBIT margin is estimated at 2 to 3 percent, which is not nearly enough in this industry.

This Canadian Tiny Home Is All About High-End Minimalism and Sophisticated Looks

Photo: Summit Tiny Homes
Canadian tiny homes are among the most rugged, durable you’ll find considering they’re built to withstand harsh winters and extreme temperatures. But Canadian builders are also known for creating some of the most beautiful tiny homes on wheels, combining high-end craftsmanship with natural wood finishes and clever space-saving designs.
The Nysos tiny home on wheels by British Columbia-based Summit Tiny Homes is a stunning example of this unique mix of resilience and gorgeous styling. It features an ingenious layout with two lofts and a downstairs bedroom, high-end materials and finishes, and a supremely modern aesthetic that makes it feel sophisticated without losing the warm, cozy ambiance tiny houses are usually known to exude.
Summit Tiny Homes has been part of the growing tiny living movement since 2017, attracting people looking to downsize and simplify their lives with designs that let you enjoy all the benefits of small-space living without making you feel like you’re downgrading. The company builds not only tiny houses on wheels but also modular homes, park models, and bespoke projects, and all of them are about high-end minimalism and quiet luxury.
The Nysos unit featured here is one of the builder’s most recent completed builds and is available for sale. It is based on a triple-axle trailer and measures 36 feet (nearly 11 meters) long and 8 feet (2.4 meters) wide, which means it doesn’t require special permits to be towed on public roads.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes One of the things that make this model stand out is that, despite its road-worthy dimensions, it is well appointed for full-time living and offers a generous layout that accommodates an open lounge, a kitchen and bathroom, and three distinct sleeping areas, making it a practical option for families or anyone who needs more sleeping capacity.
A display of modern elegance, the home’s exterior is finished with dark corrugated metal siding and natural cedar accents, along with a durable metal roof. Two entry doors and large picture windows create a seamless connection with the outdoors and allow residents to admire the Canadian landscapes.
One of the first things that catches the eye once you step inside is the rich color palette and elegant styling. Vivid blue cabinetry, white shiplap walls, and light oak accents harmonioulsy combine to create an interior that feels both contemporary and timeless. Everything is bathed in natural light, giving the space an airy ambiance, while ample storage solutions, including integrated storage stairs, built-in shelves, and wardrobe space, keep it organized and clutter-free.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes The interior layout is about convenience and functional living above all else. The open-concept kitchen and living room is the first area you step into when opening the main entry door. It’s an inviting space with striking blue cabinets in the kitchen and matching furniture in the lounge zone. It even includes cozy window seating, a full wall of custom built-in bookshelves and a fireplace, which give it a cozy mountain cabin charm.
Instead of a traditional sofa, the lounge is fitted with a built-in day bed with custom cushions, which is positioned right beneath a large window that facilitates a nature immersive living experience. The daybed even comes with integrated drawers for added storage.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Though considerably more compact than a household kitchen, the adjacent cooking space is designed to offer a similar level of functionality. The beautiful blue base cabinets are paired with gray solid surface countertops and elegant black hardware, while the white tile backsplash and oak overhead cabinets complete the sophisticated look.
It is efficiently equipped with practical appliances, including an induction cooktop, a range hood, an oven, and an apartment-size fridge. The latter is conveniently housed in a dedicated tower next to the storage staircase. There is also a stainless steel apron sink and a pantry integrated under the staircase.
Speaking of the staircase, it is designed with a combination of open cubbies under the treads and closed cabinets on the side, maximizing the use of every square inch, and comes with a beautiful vertical slat detailing. It leads to one of the two lofts, which is luminous enough and large enough to be transformed into a cozy treehouse-like bedroom.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes The other loft, located above the lounge area, is a bit smaller and is accessed via a simple ladder. It’s more open, with just basic wooden rails, and offers a flexible space for storage or extra sleeping arrangements.
But unlike many tiny houses that rely solely on lofts for sleeping accommodation, the Nysos also includes a proper main-floor bedroom. It’s not very large, but it’s definitely much more comfortable with its full standing height and room to move on two sides of the queen-size bed. It also includes a full wardrobe and a bedside ledge, and a double glass door provides access to the outdoors, turning it into a private retreat.
The bathroom inside this home is a walk-through unit that helps create privacy for the main bedroom and features a custom tiled shower and the kind of finishes that give it an upscale look. A vanity and toilet are also included, along with a washer-dryer combo that enhances everyday convenience.
Photo: Summit Tiny Homes Like all the models in Summit Tiny Homes’ lineup, the Nysos is equipped with modern systems that everyday living comfortable in any season. The home comes with LED lighting throughout, an on-demand water heater, and a heat-recovery ventilation system. For thermal comfort, it relies on a highly efficient air conditioning and a cold-climate heat pump, with the option to add in-floor heating.
The Nysos is basically a tiny home model that offers everything one could wish for in terms of tiny living, including a layout that blends openness with privacy, a supremely modern aesthetic, and ample storage solutions. This particular unit is available for immediate delivery, priced at CAD $175,000, which is about USD $122,500 at current exchange rates.

By Ian Putzger Americas correspondent
16 November 2026
As rising costs outpace rate increases, the pool of truckers in North America continues to shrink – and industry experts see no end to the bloodletting.
The C-suites of large trucking firms are, however, upbeat on their prospects.
Industry reports show a steady increase in casualties in the trucking industry: in the five weeks from mid-September into October ,at least 16 carriers filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, or simply collapsed with Chapter 7 submissions.
Bankruptcy filings have occurred all across the US, many are small and mid-sized truckers, tanging from owner-operators with a single vehicle to firms fielding 50-100 trucks, crushed by liabilities of several hundred thousand dollars up to several million.
Recent filings include Silk Route Transportation from Maryland (12 trucks in its fleet), buckling under liabilities of $541,000, and California-based Road King Transport (20 trucks), with almost $3.4m in debts.
The shrinkage of capacity, precipitated by Washington’s crusade to push non-resident truckers and drivers with inadequate English language skills out of the industry, has been lifting trucking rates, but costs for truckers have risen even faster.
Elevated fuel costs have been a heavy burden, which has fallen disproportionately on smaller outfits that do not have fuel surcharge mechanisms to mitigate the impact, as the pricing over load boards is all-inclusive.
Oil prices have retreated lately, but the outlook remains grim. The Energy Information Administration updated its projected retail prices of petrol and diesel for next year on 5 November, to an average of $5.03 per gallon of diesel, up from $4.49 in October.
Brent crude oil prices, currently around $92 a barrel, are expected to average $86 next year, but still way above 2025 levels.
According to Satish Jindel, founder and president of SJ Consulting, the hit from fuel cost is not as heavy as the rise in insurance costs in the wake of the Montgomery lawsuit ruling of May, which found brokers and 3PLs liable in cases of serious crashes involving truckers they hire. This has raised the bar for these firms to ensure carriers they use have good safety credentials and insurance.
As with fuel costs, smaller truckers are hit hardest by this, as they tend to pay the most per unit and lack the leverage of bigger competitors to negotiate insurance discounts.
Mr Jindel predicted that casualties on the trucking scene would continue, although the shrinkage of operators would maintain upward pressure on trucking rates.
“Small truckers and brokers will go out of business, but it will have no impact. Shippers may have to pay more, but freight continues to move,” he said.
Indeed, the number of trucks on US roads has not dropped as steeply as the number of trucking firms. While many operators have gone bankrupt, others have decided to put their trucks to work for larger operators, primarily mid-sized firms.
From the vantage points of the large trucking providers, the landscape looks decidedly brighter, as the shrinkage of capacity has enabled them to raise their pricing, despite sluggish demand. Recent earnings calls showed optimism.
“We believe we are still in the early innings of a multi-year upcycle,” commented Derek Leathers, CEO and president of Werner Enterprises. “Structural supply contractions continue across the industry. Customer demand remains stable, and our pricing discipline remains firm, with rates continuing to move upward toward more sustainable re-investable levels.”
And James Grant, group CFO of Covenant Logistics Group, said: “I think coming out of a four-year downcycle and moving into a stronger freight cycle, the types of opportunities that we have in front of us today are plentiful.”
Meanwhile, another potentially tectonic change appears to be closing in faster than anticipated. According to research from Kearney and the MIT Mobility Initiative, the cost of operating autonomous trucks in the US could be on a level with fielding trucks driven by humans as soon as 2028.
This year, running an autonomous truck costs around $4 a mile, compared with $2.50 a mile for human drivers, but the rates are expected to converge, as autonomous trucking costs sink to $2.60 a mile by 2028, while human truck operation costs could rise to $2.70 a mile.
The study predicts that the convergence of costs in Europe and the Middle East to play out closer to 2030 and 2032, respectively.
Mr Jindel is less sanguine on autonomous trucking, suggesting: “Today autonomous trucking is a hype. There will be an impact, but not soon.”
Regulators are not going to rush, given question marks over the safety of autonomous operations at this point, he pointed out, adding that progress in trucking would be significantly slower than with passenger vehicles, given the potentially much higher impact of an accident involving an autonomous truck.

"Full Service" Is an Insanely Luxurious Houseboat Imagined as a Floating Party Palace
54 photos
Photo: Adonia Yachts
Even the fanciest, fastest superyacht is ultimately a house that floats, packed with all the creature comforts ensuring a nice life for however long you can afford to be away. This floating house is even more house than a yacht – and the ultimate floating party palace because of it.
This is Full Service, the latest build from U.S.-based Adonia Yachts. Adonia themselves call it a "yacht," though the correct name would be a houseboat; Full Service is a fully custom, absolutely insane houseboat designed to turn family vacations in a never-ending party.
Adonia Yachts, named this way after the Greek god of beauty and desire, boasts over 20 years of houseboat manufacturing experience. To quote directly, they're "willing and ready to build your wildest dream," starting from several series models they offer, and on the condition that you can afford said dream.
The Adonia catalog includes the CX Series, the AL Series, the CT Series that you can equip with an optional helipad on top, the XL Series of houseboats with a stacked, oversize superstructure, and commercial series yachts. All these come in various lengths and serves as guidelines to any future build, so that every unit leaving their factory is 100% custom.
Photo: Adonia Yachts Highlights that you can choose include a hot tub, firepit, hydraulic docks, an extended aft deck with folding jet ski ramps, or a private movie theater. You can choose to replace walls with collapsible glass, enclose spaces or leave them open, add fueling stations, and whatever other features you deem necessary for the best vacation ever.
They don't say which series is at the base of the Full Service unit, and the build itself makes an identification impossible. However, they mention that it comes in at 77 feet (23.5 meters) of length and 12 feet (3.6 meters) of width, while the comprehensive video tour below shows it features four decks in total.
Full Service is the first houseboat Adonia built for use on Lake Havasu, AZ, but it's for a private owner, so there's no sense in starting to pinch pennies to rent it someday. It's out and about solely to be gaped at, serving as a great example of what you can achieve with the right builder and the right budget in terms of accommodation at sea.
Photo: Adonia Yachts Like all houseboats, Full Service is made only for calm waters, where it will move slowly and rarely. It's more house than a yacht in both senses: it offers more amenities and a higher sleeping capacity, but also less mobility, just like a brick-and-mortar house.
This one in particular features seven bedrooms, including the master suite that gets half of the main deck, six bathrooms, and at least three more half-baths – powder rooms or service bathrooms, however you want to call them. It also offers several lounge spaces, both indoors and outside, almost too many to count and definitely more than you have sleeping spaces .
With the communal spaces outnumbering private bedrooms, it becomes clear that Full Service was imagined as a party venue. And it delivers. Each lounge space comes complete with a full kitchen and dining spaces, loungers, and movin' and grovin' space.
Photo: Adonia Yachts The uppermost deck includes oversize loungers, a firepit, wraparound seating, and one of the two helms onboard. The second deck caters more to the indoor-outdoor crowd, though it also has a more private terrace with a chute to launch yourself to the waters below to cool off.
Also here is the first of the many kitchens, a chef's unit complete with every appliance needed, from dishwasher to barbecue and ice maker, and with an integrated dining bar. A separate dining area is also available, as is a service bathroom, and a walk-in pantry.
The master bedroom takes up half of this deck and comes with a gorgeous ensuite, lots of space, and access to a private terrace through sliding glass doors. If you're the host of this floating party and you're paying for everything, it makes sense to have the best accommodation possible.
Photo: Adonia Yachts The main deck is more of the same (another massive kitchen, another large formal dining area, and another lounge) but it also offers access to the aft beach club, which comes with an extendable section with a jet ski ramp and a dedicated 100-gallon fueling station. The deck here is lined with hatches that reveal access to large storage compartments that form the garage.
Another neat option on Full Service are the hydraulic docks with removable handrails, adding extra functionality when you dock, are pulling in on watertoys, or are at anchor on the lake.
The other six staterooms are below deck , and while they do have ensuites, they're surprisingly compact. If the idea is to offer basic sleeping accommodation for as many people people and then to have spaces where to enjoy time together, they will work just fine, though.
Photo: Adonia Yachts Full Service comes with a professional-grade audio system throughout at least two large-screen drop-down TVs in the communal spaces. There's no mention of the propulsion system , though, anywhere.
Neither is there regarding pricing. Remember, this is a fully custom build commissioned by a private owner, and as such, it would have been in bad taste for the builder to go around throwing numbers. That said, a comparable Adonia Yachts build sells on the second-hand market for upwards of $2.4 million, so don't expect this one to have cost any less.

Last month, Toyota dealers moved no fewer than 5,954 units of the Hilux in Australia, setting a new record for the month. That sales volume also secured the Hilux's eighth-highest monthly result ever, going to show that consumer demand for the new-gen model is healthy.
Better still for Toyota and the Hilux , which is a different animal from the North American-market Tacoma, the mid-size pickup has reclaimed first place in year-to-date terms. The Hilux finally managed to beat the Ford Motor Company's Ranger, with Toyota moving 1,113 more units.
The October 2026 tally represents a 34 percent increase over the 4,444 units delivered in October 2026, marking the first time the Hilux topped the monthly sales chart in 2026. Last year, it claimed the number one position five times. Indeed, the Hilux is one of the best-selling vehicles in the Land Down Under.
Looking at the bigger picture, Toyota's RAV4 claimed third place in October 2026 with 4,718 sales to its name. Introduced a year ago in Australia, Thailand, and Europe simultaneously, the ninth generation of the Hilux is the first one developed from the outset to support BEV and FCEV powertrains.
The Australian rollout took a bit longer to reach its full potential, with certain important configurations arriving at dealers in the latter part of 2026. Prospective customers, therefore, had fewer options during the first months of the ninth gen. Vehicle availability needs mentioning as well, with stock leaving much to be desired through early fall.
Photo: Toyota In any case, I would be careful about interpreting a record month as proof that the ninth-generation Hilux is a commercial success. A model that spent months waiting for allocation is capable of producing an exceedingly healthier monthly result once supply catches up, and the broader year-to-date figures reveal a far less flattering picture.
Between January 2026 and October 2026, the Hilux delivered 42,570 units in the Australian market. That's 129 vehicles behind the Ford Ranger, and the Tesla Model Y is right behind it with 39,035 deliveries through October 2025. The RAV4 is listed fourth with 35,927 sales, while China's BYD Sealion 7 has clocked 22,488 deliveries in the analyzed ten-month timeframe.
Per the Federal Chamber of Automotive Industries, legacy automakers like Toyota and Ford are facing increasingly more competition from Chinese newcomers. China served as the largest source of vehicles recorded through VFACTS in October 2026, supplying 36.3 percent of everything delivered last month. Japan followed with 23.3 percent, then Thailand with 17.9 percent.
In terms of brands, Toyota led monthly sales with 20,649 vehicles compared to 10,025 for second-placed BYD and 7,310 for Ford. As far as many observers are concerned, the all-new third-generation Audi Q7 (together with its larger Q9 sibling) has the potential to turn the tide for Audi of America, which has been slumping badly in terms of sales as of late, despite the arrival of the all-new A5 and A6 passenger cars.
But now the Audi Q7 and Q9 are seen as the heavyweights that the Ingolstadt brand needed to swing the sales around into a positive direction: the third-generation Audi Q7 has a traditional design but with numerous enhancements and gasoline plus diesel powertrains. In fact, there’s also the sporty Audi SQ7 , which packs V8 oomph under the hood, just like the Americans love to.
The massive Audi SQ7 features the company’s 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8 now packing 591 hp and 590 lb-ft of torque or 800 Nm instead of the 2.9-liter V6, and it’s going to be a tough competitor for the BMW X5 Neue Klasse and the recently facelifted Mercedes-Benz GLE and GLE Coupe. Alas, it still has the usual understated Audi looks.
But what if you don’t want to be subtle? No worries, as the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI will certainly take care of that. For example, Ildar, the virtual artist better known as " ildar_project " on social media, usually plays with tuned vehicles - so is anyone surprised by this new creation – all over again?
Initially, he created the Angry Orange Audi SQ7, packing a dual-tone orange and black widebody transformation, but now he’s back with a more serious option featuring a gray body and piano black details. He’s still giving the SQ7 a set of humongous black Y-spoke alloy wheels, though, so no one should think that he’s grown soft lately. Image: © Kateryna Chyzhevska
By Alison Koo
16 November 2026
Taiwan liner operator Wan Hai’s re-entry into the transpacific market back in 2020, was a move that has paid off, as Asia-US East Coast is now the company’s largest revenue contributor, said chairman Chen Po-ting on Friday.
Since 2020, Wan Hai has generated cumulative net profit of about TWD300bn ($9.11bn) through to Q3 26, despite recording a net loss of TWD5.8bn ($189m) during the market correction in 2023.
Mr Chen said: “We accelerated fleet expansion during the pandemic, taking a calculated risk, despite concerns among major shareholders that the market could return to normal once the health crisis subsided. We chose phased investments and continued monitoring market developments.”
Despite concerns that the current massive orderbook for new box ships could depress rates next year, since Covid the liner shipping industry had moved from monopolistic competition into orderly rivalry, he added.
Freight rates are no longer determined solely by supply and demand, with geopolitical developments, climate change, and logistical bottlenecks increasingly shaping the container shipping market.
Mr Chen asked: “Why must freight rates remain the same as before? Rising costs associated with green energy, environmental protection, and human rights are also changing the economics of shipping.”
To strengthen its long-haul routes, Wan Hai acquired second-hand ships and ordered larger vessels, and its capacity now stands at 627,456 teu, having grown by more than 132% since the pandemic, the second-largest increase among the world’s 12 biggest container shipping lines. The Taiwanese operator is the only major shipping line to operate a fully owned fleet, and does not charter any vessels.
Wan Hai will take delivery of 11 ships in 2027 – ten 16,000 teu vessels and one of 8,700 teu.
The additional capacity will support the deployment of larger vessels on routes serving the US east and west coasts, South America, the Middle East, India, and within Asia.
